reproduce.summary: e2e/code-contrast.spec.ts runs once in the dark theme and once in the light theme. It sends a message that the fake engine echoes back as markdown with inline code and a fenced code block. For both kinds of code it asserts four things: the computed `color-scheme` matches the theme, the colour equals the theme's `--foreground`, contrast is at least 4.5:1, and every request stays on localhost:5199. It should fail now because nothing sets `color-scheme`, so the computed value is "normal" and not "dark"/"light". The colour and contrast checks also catch the reported dark grey if Chrome's computed colour shows it. I haven't been able to run it.

reviewed.test_note: It covers dark and light themes and both block and inline code in the assistant answer. It checks the computed colour against the theme --foreground (#f2ebfa and #1d1b20), checks WCAG contrast against the real background, and checks that every request stays on localhost:5199. User messages are not rendered as markdown, so `.md` only matches the answer. One weakness: it also asserts `colorScheme`, which fails on the old code whatever the text colour is. So "failed before" does not prove the grey text was reproduced, which was the point of plan step 2.
reviewed.cause_note: The CSS change is what the spec asks for. `.md pre` and inline `.md code` now set `text-foreground` explicitly instead of relying on inheritance. `:root` and `.dark` now declare `color-scheme`, so browser defaults follow the theme. Nothing is tailored to the test's inputs.

findings.text: The spec asks for a `/code` command in the fake engine, listed in the header comment. It was not added. The test instead relies on the echo putting a fence at the start of a line. That works for now, but it depends on the exact echo format. The spec's file list is not followed, and this is not mentioned anywhere.

`expect(s.colorScheme).toBe(theme)` runs before the colour assertion, so on the old code the test may have failed only because `color-scheme` was missing. The diff does not show whether the grey code text (the reported bug) was actually reproduced, as plan step 2 required. Ask the author whether the colour assertion also failed before the fix.
